narration_hi_en: Pehle n aur orbital quantum number ki jodi dekho. N teen ho toh ell ki maximum value do hai. Option C mein ell teen diya hai. Isi ek check se answer mil gaya.
solution_steps: For a given n, the orbital quantum number ℓ ranges from 0 through n − 1. With n = 3, the only allowed ℓ values are 0, 1 and 2.
Option C has ℓ = 3, so it is forbidden. In the other three tuples, mℓ lies between −ℓ and +ℓ and the spin projection is an allowed −½.
stem: An electron has principal quantum number n = 3. Which tuple (n, ℓ, mℓ, ms) is forbidden?
subject: Chemistry

narration_hi_en: Saatva term beech mein hai. Pehla aur terahva, phir doosra aur baarahva, aise chhe pairs bante hain. Har pair ka sum assi hai. Chhe guna assi, aur beech ka chaalees jodo. Total paanch sau bees.
solution_steps: The seventh term lies in the middle. Each pair equally far from it has sum 2 × 40 = 80, because the two offsets cancel.
There are six such pairs and the middle term itself, giving 6 × 80 + 40 = 520.
stem: The seventh term of an arithmetic progression is 40. What is the sum of its first thirteen terms?
subject: Mathematics

narration_hi_en: Energy ko square form mein likho. X do par energy minimum hai. Thoda right le jao toh force left, aur thoda left le jao toh force right. Dono taraf se force do ki taraf hai, isliye equilibrium stable hai.
solution_steps: Complete the square. U(x) = (x − 2)² − 4, so x = 2 is the minimum of the potential energy.
The force is F = −dU/dx = −2(x − 2). It vanishes at 2 and points back toward 2 on either side. The equilibrium is stable.
stem: A particle moves along one axis with potential energy U(x) = x² − 4x in the chosen units. What kind of equilibrium does it have at x = 2?
subject: Physics

narration_hi_en: Current aur time multiply karke 965 coulomb milte hain. Yeh zero point zero one mole electrons hai. Har silver ion ek electron leta hai, toh silver ka mass 1.08 gram hai.
solution_steps: Charge passed = current × time = 1.93 × 500 = 965 C, or 0.0100 mol of electrons.
Each Ag⁺ takes one electron. Silver deposited = 0.0100 × 108 = 1.08 g.
stem: A cell carries a steady current of 1.93 A for 500 s through AgNO₃ solution. Find the mass of silver deposited. Assume 100% current efficiency, F = 96,500 C/mol and Ag = 108 g/mol.
subject: Chemistry

narration_hi_en: Series mein dono cells ko same charge milta hai. Silver se electron moles nikalte hain. Copper two plus ke liye do electrons chahiye, isliye copper ka mass zero point six four gram hai.
solution_steps: Series cells receive the same charge. Silver deposited = 2.16 ÷ 108 = 0.020 mol, so 0.020 mol of electrons passed.
Each Cu²⁺ requires two electrons. Copper formed = (0.020 ÷ 2) × 64 = 0.64 g.
stem: Two electrolysis cells are connected in series. The first deposits 2.16 g of silver from Ag⁺ and the second deposits copper from Cu²⁺. How much copper forms? Assume 100% current efficiency. Use Ag = 108 and Cu = 64 g/mol.
subject: Chemistry

narration_hi_en: Pehle poore charge se theoretical mass nikalo. Nickel two plus ke liye do electrons lagenge, toh theoretical yield 1.18 gram hai. Actual ko theoretical se divide karke sau se multiply karo. Efficiency assi percent hai.
solution_steps: The charge corresponds to 3,860 ÷ 96,500 = 0.040 mol of electrons.
The theoretical nickel yield is (0.040 ÷ 2) × 59 = 1.18 g.
Current efficiency = (0.944 ÷ 1.18) × 100 = 80%.
stem: A nickel-plating cell deposits 0.944 g of nickel from Ni²⁺ using 3,860 C. What is its current efficiency, expressed as a percentage? Use Ni = 59 g/mol and F = 96,500 C/mol.
subject: Chemistry

narration_hi_en: Aluminium three plus ko teen electrons chahiye. Metal ke moles ko teen se multiply karo aur phir Faraday constant se. 9650 coulomb ko 9.65 ampere se divide karne par ek hazaar second aate hain.
solution_steps: 0.90 ÷ 27 = 1/30 mol of aluminium. Each aluminium ion takes three electrons.
Required charge = (3/30) × 96,500 = 9,650 C.
Time = charge ÷ current = 9,650 ÷ 9.65 = 1,000 s.
stem: Aluminium is deposited from molten Al³⁺ salt using a current of 9.65 A. How many seconds are needed to deposit 0.90 g of Al at 100% efficiency? Use Al = 27 g/mol and F = 96,500 C/mol.
subject: Chemistry

narration_hi_en: Sum aath diya hai, toh sample space sirf paanch ordered pairs ka hai. Teen pehle aaye ya baad mein, dono cases count honge. Probability do bate paanch.
solution_steps: The ordered pairs with sum 8 are (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3) and (6,2). All five are equally likely.
Two pairs contain a 3, giving conditional probability 2/5.
stem: A fair die is rolled twice. You learn that the sum is 8. What is the probability that at least one roll was 3?
subject: Mathematics

narration_hi_en: Red milne ka chance dono boxes ke liye alag hai. A aur red ka joint chance teen bate aath hai. Ise red ke total chance se divide karo. Answer nau bate terah.
stem: Box A holds three red and one blue token. Box B holds one red and two blue tokens. A fair coin chooses the box, then one token is drawn uniformly. Given a red token, what is the probability it came from A?
subject: Mathematics

narration_hi_en: Condition ke baad sirf chaar odd cards bachte hain. Chhe possible pairs mein se ek-saat aur teen-paanch ka sum aath hai. Do bate chhe, yaani ek bate teen.
solution_steps: The odd cards are 1, 3, 5 and 7. They give six equally likely unordered pairs.
Only (1,7) and (3,5) sum to 8. The required probability is 2/6 = 1/3.
stem: Two distinct cards are drawn uniformly without replacement from cards numbered 1 through 8. Given that both cards are odd, what is the probability that their sum is 8?
subject: Mathematics

narration_hi_en: At least one head diya hai, toh teen tails wala outcome hata do. Saat mein se teen outcomes mein exactly do heads hain. Probability teen bate saat.
solution_steps: Of the eight equally likely three-toss outcomes, remove TTT. Seven remain.
Exactly two heads occur in HHT, HTH and THH, so the conditional probability is 3/7.
stem: A fair coin is tossed three times. Given that at least one head occurs, what is the probability that exactly two heads occur?
subject: Mathematics

narration_hi_en: Paani mein bead 18 centimetre neeche dikhta hai. Yeh apparent depth hai. Asli depth ke liye 18 ko chaar bate teen se multiply karo. Answer 24 centimetre. Chhe centimetre sirf shift hai.
solution_steps: At near-normal viewing from air, apparent depth = real depth ÷ refractive index.
Real depth = 18 × (4/3) = 24 cm. The bead looks 6 cm closer to the surface.
stem: A bead looks 18 cm below a flat water surface when viewed almost vertically from air. Water has refractive index 4/3. How far below the surface is the bead actually?
subject: Physics

narration_hi_en: Ab scratch apni asli position se chaar centimetre upar dikhta hai. Microscope ko bhi chaar centimetre upar le jao. Baarah centimetre surface se image ki depth hai.
solution_steps: The apparent depth below the water surface is 16 ÷ (4/3) = 12 cm.
The image is 16 − 12 = 4 cm above the scratch. Raise the microscope by 4 cm to focus on the image.
stem: A travelling microscope is focused on a scratch on the floor of an empty tank. The tank is then filled with 16 cm of water. In which direction and by how much should the microscope move to refocus? View vertically from air and use refractive index 4/3.
subject: Physics

narration_hi_en: Do layers hain. Har layer ki apparent thickness alag nikalo. Oil ke aath centimetre aur paani ke baarah centimetre jodo. Mark bees centimetre neeche dikhega.
solution_steps: For parallel flat layers viewed from air near the normal, add each layer's thickness divided by its refractive index.
Oil contributes 12 ÷ (3/2) = 8 cm. Water contributes 16 ÷ (4/3) = 12 cm.
Apparent depth below the oil surface = 8 + 12 = 20 cm.
stem: A flat tank has 12 cm of oil above 16 cm of water. A small mark is on its floor. From air, looking almost vertically down, find the apparent depth of the mark in cm. Use refractive indices 3/2 for oil and 4/3 for water.
subject: Physics

narration_hi_en: Nau centimetre shift hai. Ise depth mat samjho. Sattaais mein se nau ghatao, toh apparent depth athaarah hai. Index sattaais bate athaarah, yaani dedh.
solution_steps: Apparent depth = real depth − upward shift = 27 − 9 = 18 cm.
Refractive index = real depth ÷ apparent depth = 27 ÷ 18 = 1.50.
stem: A mark lies 27 cm below a liquid surface. Viewed almost normally from air, it appears shifted upward by 9 cm. What is the liquid's refractive index?
subject: Physics
